key_insight: BridgeSRDA combines low-resolution forecasts and sparse observations to generate high-resolution flow ensembles, approaching high-resolution filtering accuracy at lower computational cost.
engineering_relevance: The framework could make probabilistic flow-state reconstruction more affordable by replacing repeated high-resolution ensemble forecasts with low-resolution forecasts and learned stochastic transport.
method: Condition learned stochastic transport on low-resolution forecasts and sparse, noisy observations.
Sample high-resolution analysis ensembles, retrospective reconstructions, and short-range nowcasts.
Use each current analysis to initialize the next low-resolution forecast.
evidence_signal: Across ten independently initialized 3D quasi-geostrophic trajectories in a narrow-jet regime different from training, BridgeSRDA reduced the mean absolute error ratio by approximately 32.5% versus deterministic 4D SRDA and took approximately 17 s per 30-member analysis versus 31 s for a high-resolution ensemble filter.
watch_item: Uncertainty remains undercalibrated: nominal 90% intervals covered approximately 62% of reference values, with boundary spread artifacts and reduced skill under sparser observations.
paper_title: BridgeSRDA: Efficient Probabilistic Super-Resolution Data Assimilation with Forecast-Informed Stochastic Interpolants
